The run and the orchestration graph

Signing starts the run; watching it is optional. The run view appears in the space with the orchestration graph: one node per execution unit, edges for the order the engine derived. Each card — worker, auditor and the closing gate alike — is titled with the promise it is keeping, in your own words; the worker id and the full promise sentence move to the card’s hover text, so the title reads as what is being built rather than as a raw id.

Live state is never carried by colour alone. Every card wears a coloured frame and a short state word — ready, running, needs you, passed, failed, never ran — and both survive zooming out, at the point where the card’s chips are dropped for space. A card that is part of the signed work being built now carries a separate gold mark saying "cut" — a different fact from its live state, so a card can be both in the cut and running at once without either mark hiding the other. Click a node for its detail; the log tail runs beneath; Stop aborts every live worker. The closing gate’s own card opens its own log the same way, on the same single click as every worker card.

How the machine builds

  • Tests first, blind. For each acceptance criterion a probe author writes an executable check — in a detached snapshot of the branch where the implementation-in-progress does not exist. Blinding is structural, not a promise in a prompt. Finished probes persist in a durable store.

  • Roles own paths. Every test-shaped path a promise lands in — an existing test the change tightens, a standing check that is itself the deliverable — belongs to the tester, who brings it under the criteria before the code exists, and records every choice the contract forced (a name, a literal, a rule) as a DECISION. The coder’s footprint holds production paths only; it never reads or writes a test. A plan that hands a coder a test is refused before any worker starts.

  • The coder builds against the brief, with your ask verbatim as the north star, your decisions in force attached, and the tester’s decisions as contract. It has a real verify tool: an isolated runner overlays its current work with the held-out probes and returns per-criterion PASS/FAIL with evidence.

  • Green is decided by the oracle, not the worker. A unit completes only when the checks are green for its current state (MANDATORY-GREEN). Not green routes a bounded rework carrying the oracle’s evidence.

  • A supervisor with both sides of the wall audits whether the brief contains every fact the checks require — before the coder spends anything, and again when the same failure repeats. A disclosure is by definition a contract gap and is recorded in the defect ledger.

  • Containment. A worker that writes outside its declared footprint has the stray paths reverted and the run halts, named.

  • Parallel frontier. Ready units run concurrently (the maxConcurrent setting); slices commit on the branch as they finish.

  • A worker’s question goes to the machine first. The supervisor, who sees the brief, the checks and the repository, answers whatever the run itself can decide and the worker resumes. Only a question about intent — a choice among behaviours your asks do not decide — reaches you, in your own words; you are never asked about files, names or tools.

The delivery

The closing gate re-runs every probe from a clean environment, the honesty scan reads the delivered files for self-declared deferrals, the repository’s own suite runs, and the branch becomes a pull request whose description carries every acceptance criterion of the cut with its verdict — including "not checked" for a criterion nothing judged — the tester’s decisions and every UNDELIVERED line. The same complete list is what the delivery page shows, so the pull request and the delivery page never disagree about a criterion. The machine face — the structured verification trace — persists in the store beside the space.

A run ends in exactly one of three states:

delivered

every promise kept and the product builds. Anything the machine could not settle rides the page as a finding for you to weigh; see The two gates.

withheld

a promise could not be kept after every repairer was spent, or the product does not build. The branch keeps the work and the record keeps the verdict; nothing is handed over for you to finish, and the way back in is offered.

halted

the run went quiet long enough that the watchdog ended it, and said which units were open and what each was waiting for.

A withheld run is still a run and its report still names itself. The delivery is never silently downgraded and never silently abandoned.
